title: 'Scrubs' Revival Shakes Up Cast for Season 2 as Show Targets Fall Debut
excerpt: Joel Kim Booster and X Mayo are departing while Ava Bunn earns a promotion ahead of the hit comedy's 10-episode second season on ABC.
body:
• Joel Kim Booster (Dr. Kevin Park) and X Mayo (Nurse Pippa Raymond) are both departing the Scrubs revival ahead of its second season.
  • Ava Bunn, who plays intern Dr. Sam Tosh, has been promoted from recurring player to series regular.
  • Season 2 will consist of 10 episodes and is slated for ABC's fall 2026 lineup in its Wednesday 8 p.m. timeslot.
  • Original stars Zach Braff, Donald Faison and Sarah Chalke return as leads, with Neil Flynn and Rachel Bilson also coming back.

ABC's Scrubs revival is undergoing a significant cast shake-up ahead of its second season, with Joel Kim Booster and X Mayo both exiting the series, according to Deadline. Booster played attending physician Dr. Kevin Park and Mayo portrayed Nurse Pippa Raymond during the show's first season, which premiered in February and became one of the top-rated new comedies on broadcast television.

In a more encouraging move for fans, Ava Bunn — who played intern Dr. Sam Tosh in a recurring capacity — has been promoted to series regular for Season 2. The change signals the show's intention to invest more deeply in its newer characters as the revival continues to balance nostalgia with fresh storytelling.

The Returning Guard

The show's three leads remain in place. Zach Braff returns as J.D., now Chief of Medicine at Sacred Heart Hospital, alongside Donald Faison as Turk and Sarah Chalke as Elliot. John C. McGinley, whose schedule limited his Season 1 availability due to commitments to Bill Lawrence's other series Rooster, is expected to have an expanded presence as Dr. Perry Cox.

Other returning cast members include Judy Reyes as Carla Espinosa, Vanessa Bayer as wellness coordinator Sibby, Robert Maschio as The Todd, and Michael James Scott as Nurse Dubois — all in recurring roles. Christa Miller returns as a guest star playing Jordan Sullivan.

Two familiar faces from the original series are also returning. Neil Flynn, who played the Janitor throughout the show's initial run, appeared in the Season 1 finale and will return in a recurring capacity. Rachel Bilson, who debuted as gift shop worker Charlie in the finale, will also be back, continuing a romantic storyline with J.D.

The Kelso Question

One notable absence from the casting announcements is Ken Jenkins, who played the acerbic Dr. Bob Kelso across all nine seasons of the original Scrubs. Series creator Bill Lawrence told Deadline earlier this year that Kelso would return in Season 2, but Jenkins' name has not appeared in any official cast list so far.

Andy Ridings, who appeared in three episodes as Wes — a pilot who dates Elliot — also has an uncertain status, with producers reportedly undecided on whether to bring the character back.

A Quick Turnaround

ABC greenlit the second season just two weeks after the Season 1 finale aired in April. The network originally launched the revival as a midseason entry, but moved Season 2 to its fall 2026 lineup — a notably fast turnaround in an era when many shows wait a year or more between seasons.

"We love the momentum on Scrubs. It was the No. 1 new comedy on a multiplatform basis, the No. 1 comedy in 18-49 on linear this season."

— Ari Goldman, ABC scheduling executive

Season 2 will run for 10 episodes, up from nine in the first season, and will air Wednesdays at 8 p.m. ET/PT, followed by Abbott Elementary, Celebrity Jeopardy and Shark Tank. Showrunner Aseem Batra returns, with Mike Royce joining the executive producing team.

Looking Ahead

The revival's first season landed among the top 25 broadcast shows of the 2025-2026 season, according to Nielsen data — a strong showing for a returning property that originally ended in 2010. The Season 1 finale left several threads open, including Cox's autoimmune diagnosis, which J.D. tried to keep from Jordan, and the broader question of how Sacred Heart's veteran doctors balance their own evolving lives with mentoring a new class of interns.

For the Indian diaspora audience that grew up watching Scrubs during its 2001-2010 run, the revival's continued success points to the enduring appeal of a show that found humor and humanity in hospital hallways. Season 2 arrives this fall on ABC, with episodes streaming on Disney+ and Hulu.
